newsitem.title: USA: Most US spot resids inch up again, helped by crude.
newsitem.headline: Most US spot resids inch up again, helped by crude.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices, again helped by another rally in crude, mostly inched higher Tuesday despite skepticism that current levels could hold with almost no utility demand to lend support.

"Some people were trying to talk lower numbers, but it's tough to be bearish with crude running up again," said one cash trader, noting cheap gas and mild East Coast weather have sharply cut utility fuel oil needs.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was talked slightly higher at about $19 a barrel, traders said.
Traders said there was no word on a New York Power Authority tender for 300,000 barrels of 0.3 percent high pour for any-Oct delivery. Fixed-price bids were due Tuesday.
NYH high sulphurs notionally were unchanged, with three percent still straddling $16.75.

At the U.S. Gulf Coast, one percent gained 35 cents to the $17.50 area. USG three percent eased slightly to about $16.75. While some thought three percent was even lower, others cited talk of some Venezuelan interest for USG HSFO barrels.
October New York city gate gas was talked in the $2.05-2.10/mmBtu area versus NYH one percent resid at a $3.02/mmBtu equivalent.
